Description:
In all cases examined (Pub1 IDR, eIF4GII IDR, Lsm4 IDR, Tia1 IDR, Fus IDR, and hnRNPA1 IDR), solutions of these proteins remained clear at room temperature under physiological salt conditions (100–150 mM NaCl).
However, when the NaCl concentration was diluted to 37.5 mM, solutions of hnRNPA1IDR, eIF4GIIIDR, and FusIDR (6–33 mM protein) solutions became opalescent, and brightly fluorescent, micron-sized, spherical liquid-droplets were observed by light microscopy. Overtime, these structures settled onto the slide, where they sometimes spread into irregular shapes.
These structures appeared to be phase-separated liquids based on several criteria. They (1)were spherical in solution, (2) could flow and fuse (Movies S1 and S2), (3) showed concentration dependence in their total volume (data not shown but as explained later), and (4) disassembled rapidly when returned to high salt after 30' of low salt treatment (described later).
Solutions of Lsm4IDR, Pub1IDR, and Tia1IDR either rapidly formed fiber-like structures (Lsm4) or remained as a single phase. Thus, IDRs can alternatively form both fibers and phase-separated droplets under low salt conditions.

The addition of NPM1 to pre-formed, rpL5/rRNA puncta caused spontaneous formation of large droplets under conditions of both limiting and excess rpL5, whose sizes increased with increasing NPM1 concentration.

Finally, addition of the △N construct, lacking the OD and therefore displaying dramatically reduced multivalency, failed to cause phase separation under both excess and limiting rpL5 conditions

Consistent with the increased concentration of molecules incorporated in the dense-phase, light-phase concentrations decreased.

Description: As the starting concentration of SURF6 N increased, so did its concentration within droplets. This suggests that NPM1 responds to a broad range of concentrations of R-motif-containing proteins to form phase-separated scaffolds with different blends of homotypic and heterotypic interactions. FRAP analysis of the droplets formed with different SURF6 N:NPM1 ratios revealed that a large portion of NPM1 molecules are immobile at all ratios. However, NPM1 became more mobile inside droplets with higher SURF6 N:NPM1 ratios, as indicated by the increased mobile fraction (32% for homotypic vs. 70% for a SURF6 N:NPM1 of 4:1). These results suggest that the diffusing NPM1 molecules are less dynamic within the homotypic vs. the heterotypic scaffold. Similarly, the mobile fraction of SURF6 N also increased from 0.64 to 0.97 with the increase in SURF6 N:NPM1 ratios, indicating that, while SURF6 N remained dynamic irrespective of the SURF6 N content, the nature of the scaffold experienced changes.

Description: Co-addition of EPG-2 reduced the size of droplets formed by PGL-1/-3 and SEPA-1. The EPG-2-containing droplets remained small even 12 hr after formation, and their fusion was greatly inhibited. Addition of EPG-2 into pre-formed SEPA-1/PGL-1/-3 droplets also inhibited their further growth in size. Using EPG-2::GFP, we found that EPG-2 did not mix into the SEPA-1/PGL-1/-3 droplets, but non-homogeneously coated the surface of the droplets. EPG-2::GFP also enveloped pre-formed SEPA-1/PGL-1/-3 droplets. EPG-2 increases the salt resistance of SEPA-1/PGL-1/-3 droplets. EPG-2/SEPA-1/PGL-1/-3 liquid-like droplets develop gel-like characteristics over time.

Description: Mixing pure C. reinhardtii Rubisco (CrRubisco) and EPYC1 led to immediate formation of a turbid solution that cleared over time. The turbidity was caused by the formation of spherical droplets from the bulk solution that could be labeled by including a fluorescent EPYC1-GFP fusion protein in the reaction and occurred within seconds. The observed clearance of the solution was caused by fusion of the droplets into a large homogeneous droplet (coalescence), supporting their liquid nature. Demixed droplets could be harvested by centrifugation, and SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) analysis confirmed that both EPYC1 and Rubisco had entered the droplets. Phase separation was protein concentration-dependent and salt (but not detergent)-sensitive.

Description: Mixing pure C. reinhardtii Rubisco (CrRubisco) and EPYC1 led to immediate formation of a turbid solution that cleared over time. The turbidity was caused by the formation of spherical droplets from the bulk solution that could be labeled by including a fluorescent EPYC1-GFP fusion protein in the reaction and occurred within seconds. Description: Even the single-repeat EPYC1Δ2-4 was able to demix with Rubisco, suggesting this minimal fragment still contributes at least two Rubisco binding sites. However, droplets formed using lower-valency fragments were flatter upon contacting the coverslip than those containing more repeats indicating that the valency affects droplet surface tension. Additionally, EPYC1-GFP spiked into droplets formed with EPYC1Δ2-4 displayed higher mobility as measured by FRAP. EPYC1 variants containing three to five repeats were able to sediment Rubisco equally well as EPYC1 in our system and we could thus not detect the hypothesized magic number effect. Even the variant containing two repeats (EPYC1Δ2/3) allows almost EPYC1-like demixing, when corrected for the number of EPYC1 repeats present. In contrast the minimal construct EPYC1Δ2-4 required high Rubisco concentrations to effectively demix the enzyme. In summary, higher numbers of interaction sites in longer EPYC1 variants shift the phase diagram, permitting demixing to occur at lower protein concentrations.

Further, in the presence of both PEG 8000 and heparin, tau droplets were formed but the K274Q-tau droplets were bigger than the WT-tau droplets. Heparin alone did not form droplets. The finding indicated that the K274Q mutation decreases the critical concentration for the phase separation of tau.

Description: Freshly prepared solutions of recombinant full-length tau (tau441) in HEPES buffer (pH 7.4) at a wide range of protein concentrations (2-100 µM) show no measurable turbidity, indicating the presence of a protein (likely monomeric) in a single phase. However, upon addition to tau441 of polyethylene glycol (PEG), the volume-excluding polymer frequently used to mimic intracellular crowding, we observed a rapid increase in sample turbidity, strongly suggesting LLPS. This turbidity increase was clearly detectable at a protein concentration as low as 2 µM. Importantly, under all conditions tested, the effect showed a strong dependence on the ionic strength of the buffer, with higher amounts of PEG required to induce LLPS in the presence of increasing concentrations of NaCl.

Description: The propensity of ∆2N tau to undergo LLPS was diminished, as indicated by lower turbidity and requirement for higher concentrations of the crowding agent as compared to that for tau441. However, droplets still could be observed for this variant by microscopy, especially at higherconcentrations of PEG. Building on this finding, next we performed experiments with the N-truncated variant tau ∆1-117, in which the entire negatively charged segment has been removed. This deletion resulted in an essentially complete loss of ability to undergo LLPS, further reinforcing our central hypothesis regarding the crucial role of intermolecular electrostatic interactions between oppositely charged regions of tau. Consistent with this notion, no phase separation was observed for the negatively charged N-terminal fragment (tau ∆118-441) alone. Deletion of the entire four-repeat (4R) region (residues 244-369) modestly decreased the propensity of tau to undergo LLPS, as indicated by reduced sample turbidity, but droplets still could be observed by microscopy. This suggests that the repeats, a region critical for pathological aggregation of tau, are not essential for LLPS. Most C-terminal 402-441 segment that is predominantly negatively charged (especially within residues 418-434) appears to play a minor role, as deletion of this entire segment (tau∆402-441) had little effect on LLPS.

Description: The rPrP90-231 phase separates in vitro into micrometer-sized spherical condensates with varying diameters in water and buffer. Phase separation occurred even in the absence of macromolecular crowding agents, albeit 10% PEG 4000 increased the droplets diameter compared to rPrP90-231 in water, probably aiding the fusion of condensates. Larger rPrP90-231 condensates were observed reaching approximately 100 μm of diameter. Coalescence into large droplets is thermodynamically driven since the net surface tension is diminished over small condensates; ie, Ostwald ripening. However, the number of droplets was significantly decreased in both buffer and in the presence of PEG compared to water, suggesting dependence of phase separation behavior on ionic strength.

Description: we checked whether the rPrP90-231 liquid condensates can transit to solid-like material over time. Within the period of 20 minutes, we observed tiny bright dots on the surface of rPrP90-231 droplets in 10 mM Tris (pH 7.4), 100 mM NaCl. After 60 minutes, filamentous-like “substructures” were evident on the surface of large rPrP90-231 condensates in water, reflect- ing that biophysical properties of droplets may change over time. After 6 hours, the liquid droplets assumed characteris- tics of “aged” droplets, such as a darkly refractile appearance and the presence of aggregates sticking out of the condensate, and the same sameple after 6 h does not show intrinsic fluoresence.

Description: The ThT fluorescence curves shown in Fig. 3 demonstrate that, for all tau441 variants studied, LLPS results in a dramatic acceleration of the fibrillation reaction. For the wild-type protein, the lag phase of the reaction under LLPS conditions was ~16 h. In sharp contrast, no measurable increase in ThT fluorescence intensity was observed up to at least 40 h for the reaction in the absence of LLPS. This effect was even stronger for the mutant proteins . For example, for the P301L variant, the lag phase was reduced from ~17 h in the absence of LLPS to ~3 h in the droplet environment, and the rate of the growth phase was also greatly increased. The rate of fibrillation under LLPS conditions was especially high for the ΔK280 variant. In the latter case, the reaction (without any measurable lag phase) was essentially completed within 30 min, in sharp contrast to the lack of any ThT fluorescence increase up to at least 40 h in the absence of LLPS. The final ThT intensities at the end of the growth phase under LLPS conditions were different for individual tau variants.Importantly, consistent with the ThT data, no fibrillar structures were observed in AFM images for individual proteins at the same time points under the conditions of no LLPS.

Description:
In all cases examined (Pub1 IDR, eIF4GII IDR, Lsm4 IDR, Tia1 IDR, Fus IDR, and hnRNPA1 IDR), solutions of these proteins remained clear at room temperature under physiological salt conditions (100–150 mM NaCl).
However, when the NaCl concentration was diluted to 37.5 mM, solutions of hnRNPA1IDR, eIF4GIIIDR, and FusIDR (6–33 mM protein) solutions became opalescent, and brightly fluorescent, micron-sized, spherical liquid-droplets were observed by light microscopy. Overtime, these structures settled onto the slide, where they sometimes spread into irregular shapes.
These structures appeared to be phase-separated liquids based on several criteria. They (1)were spherical in solution, (2) could flow and fuse (Movies S1 and S2), (3) showed concentration dependence in their total volume (data not shown but as explained later), and (4) disassembled rapidly when returned to high salt after 30' of low salt treatment (described later).
Solutions of Lsm4IDR, Pub1IDR, and Tia1IDR either rapidly formed fiber-like structures (Lsm4) or remained as a single phase. Thus, IDRs can alternatively form both fibers and phase-separated droplets under low salt conditions.

Description: In the absence of PEG 8000 or heparin, tau failed to form droplets. However, tau was found to form droplets in the presence of PEG 8000 or heparin indicating the LLPS of tau. The finding indicated that the K274Q mutation decreases the critical concentration for the phase separation of tau.

Description: The propensity of ∆2N tau to undergo LLPS was diminished, as indicated by lower turbidity and requirement for higher concentrations of the crowding agent as compared to that for tau441. However, droplets still could be observed for this variant by microscopy, especially at higherconcentrations of PEG. Building on this finding, next we performed experiments with the N-truncated variant tau ∆1-117, in which the entire negatively charged segment has been removed. This deletion resulted in an essentially complete loss of ability to undergo LLPS, further reinforcing our central hypothesis regarding the crucial role of intermolecular electrostatic interactions between oppositely charged regions of tau. Consistent with this notion, no phase separation was observed for the negatively charged N-terminal fragment (tau ∆118-441) alone. Deletion of the entire four-repeat (4R) region (residues 244-369) modestly decreased the propensity of tau to undergo LLPS, as indicated by reduced sample turbidity, but droplets still could be observed by microscopy. This suggests that the repeats, a region critical for pathological aggregation of tau, are not essential for LLPS. Most C-terminal 402-441 segment that is predominantly negatively charged (especially within residues 418-434) appears to play a minor role, as deletion of this entire segment (tau∆402-441) had little effect on LLPS.

Description: we utilized salts from the Hofmeister series that have been shown to stabilize or destabilize hydrophobic interactions based on their differential ability to remove water from protein surfaces. We measured the extent of phase separation of FUS LC in varying concentrations of monovalent Hofmeister cations and anions. The Hofmeister cations had little effect on LLPS of FUS LC, likely owing to their similar interactions with water.however, phase separation of FUS LC in the presence of the monovalent anions of the same ionic strength followed the expected Hofmeister trend. Relative to sodium chloride, phase separation was nearly completely abrogated in the chaotropic salts sodium iodide and bromide, whereas phase separation in the kosmotropic salt sodium fluoride was enhanced. Therefore, hydrophobic interactions, particularly from tyrosine residues, contribute to and help stabilize FUS LLPS.

Description: First, although the IDRs itself is a low-complexity region, incubation of STT1 or STT2 individually with LTP did not form spherical droplets, but produced only irregular aggregates, indicating that the prerequisite for the occurrence of liquid-liquid phase separation is the formation of STT oligomers. Moreover, when the residues of electropositive regions within the ellipsoidal structure of individual STT1 or STT2 were changed to alanines to inhibit the formation of STT oligomers, the resulting STT mutant complex could only form smaller droplets with LTP peptide. When all the conserved positive residues of the STT electropositive regions were mutated, the resulting STT mutant complex could not induce phase transition after mixing with LTP, consistent with the implication that formation of oligomers is required for phase transition upon binding to LTP. Second, compared to LTP, the STT complex formed more and larger liquid droplets with TP (transit peptide) in the same buffer. However, the STT complex formed only tiny droplets with the inactive variant signal peptide in which the arginines of the RR motif or the hydrophobic residues of the H domain were changed to alanines, and the droplets were clearly absent when both the RR motif and H domain were mutated. Substitution of the residues of the LTP binding motif  within the STTs prevented phase separation. Thus, besides formation of STT oligomers, the STTs-LTP binding reaction is also required for this phase separation. These results suggest that multivalent electrostatic interactions and hydrophobic interactions between STT1, STT2, and LTP drive liquid-liquid phase separation.

Description: The ThT fluorescence curves shown in Fig. 3 demonstrate that, for all tau441 variants studied, LLPS results in a dramatic acceleration of the fibrillation reaction. For the wild-type protein, the lag phase of the reaction under LLPS conditions was ~16 h. In sharp contrast, no measurable increase in ThT fluorescence intensity was observed up to at least 40 h for the reaction in the absence of LLPS. This effect was even stronger for the mutant proteins . For example, for the P301L variant, the lag phase was reduced from ~17 h in the absence of LLPS to ~3 h in the droplet environment, and the rate of the growth phase was also greatly increased. The rate of fibrillation under LLPS conditions was especially high for the ΔK280 variant. In the latter case, the reaction (without any measurable lag phase) was essentially completed within 30 min, in sharp contrast to the lack of any ThT fluorescence increase up to at least 40 h in the absence of LLPS. The final ThT intensities at the end of the growth phase under LLPS conditions were different for individual tau variants.Importantly, consistent with the ThT data, no fibrillar structures were observed in AFM images for individual proteins at the same time points under the conditions of no LLPS.
